2884: Situation 1 · A colleague with suicidal ideation
2885: The person may be in intense emotional distress, feeling hopeless, empty or without a way out.
2886: They may feel isolated, misunderstood or a “burden” to others.
2887: Their ability to think clearly may be reduced and they may have difficulty identifying or expressing emotional needs.
2888: Demanding personal or professional situations may contribute to a state of great emotional dysregulation.
2890: Establish contact and presence: Approach calmly and respectfully. “Can I stay with you for a while?”
2891: Ensure safety: Take the person to a quieter space and reduce stimuli and pressure.
2892: Assess needs: Ask in a simple way, for example, “What is hardest for you right now?”
2893: Listen with empathy: Listen without interrupting, judging or correcting. “I imagine this is weighing on you heavily.”
2894: Support immediate needs: Presence, water, helping to contact someone. Small gestures make a difference.
2895: Connect with resources: Encourage professional help and offer concrete help (e.g. accompanying them, making contact easier).
2896: Promote hope: “You don’t have to deal with this alone”, “There is support available”.

2898: What to avoid and when to refer
2899: Forcing the person to talk or open up.
2901: Judging or trying to “teach a lesson”.
2904: Promising absolute confidentiality when there is a risk.

2912: Situation 2 · When a suicide occurs in the workplace
2913: The team may be in shock or emotionally disorganised.
2914: Emotions such as guilt, sadness, confusion and fear may be present.
2915: A feeling of a lack of safety in the workplace.
2916: A need for safety, stability and meaning.
2919: Establish presence and safe communication: Clear, respectful and simple communication. Show availability.
2920: Ensure emotional safety: Reduce rumours and uncertainty. Create an environment of respect and non-judgement.
2921: Assess needs: Find out who is most affected. Ask “How are you coping with this situation?”
2922: Support immediate needs: Flexibility, breaks, practical support. Presence and support between colleagues.
2923: Connect with resources: Provide psychological support. Make it easier to access help.
2924: Promote hope and normalisation: “It’s natural to have many different reactions”, “You don’t have to go through this alone”.
2925: Situation 2: what to avoid and when to refer
2926: Speculation or looking for who is to blame.
2929: Pressure to “get back to normal quickly”.

2951: When informal support is no longer enough
2952: Referral happens when informal support, such as Psychological First Aid, is no longer enough to meet the person’s needs. In these cases, it becomes important to involve specialist resources, ensuring continuity of care, protection and appropriate follow-up.
